candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11 / PDF p.15
candidate.educational_objective: Use gentle cleansing and moisture-barrier protection to reduce skin injury from repeated incontinence exposure.

options.A: Gently cleanse after incontinence and apply a moisture-barrier product to the exposed skin
options.B: Leave stool on the skin until the next scheduled bath to minimize friction
options.C: Scrub the area vigorously after each episode to remove all residual moisture
options.D: Apply a barrier product but omit cleansing after future incontinence episodes

candidate.rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition, identifies prolonged moisture exposure as a skin-breakdown risk and recommends keeping skin free of excess moisture and using moisture-barrier ointments in areas subject to moisture. Barrier protection complements, rather than replaces, appropriate cleansing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports minimizing excess moisture and use of protective moisture barriers in skin exposed to incontinence/moisture.
candidate.source_locator: Part X Integumentary > Exposure to Moisture; selected interventions to preserve skin integrity
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client has frequent loose-stool incontinence and intact but repeatedly moist perianal skin. Which nursing intervention best helps protect the skin?
